title: Internet Advertising and the Generalized Second-Price Auction
source_inventory_policy: Curated from the local NBER source text cache. Main source targets are the main-text first-price/GSP examples, Remarks 1--3, Definition 4, Lemmas 5--6, Theorem 7, Theorem 8 proof-step claims, and the bundled Theorem 8 ex-post payoff-game endpoint. Finite source-event and belief-source-extensive rows are proof-support rows rather than separate source statements.

definition4_locally_envy_free.statement: Definition 4 defines a locally envy-free equilibrium of the static GSP game as an equilibrium in which no player can improve by exchanging bids with the player ranked one position above; formally, for each allocated adjacent position the adjacent no-envy inequality holds.

stable_assignment.statement: The paper maps GSP outcomes to the Shapley-Shubik assignment game, where advertiser-position pair values are alpha_k s_i and stability means no profitable advertiser-position rematch.

first_price_running_example_profitable_r.statement: In the Section 2.2 first-price running example with two slots, click rates 200 and 100, and bidder values 10, 4, and 2, bidder 1 prefers the minimal top bid 2.02 to paying more for the same top slot, bidder 2 can profitably raise from 2.01 to 2.03 to take the top slot, and bidder 1 can then profitably raise to 2.04 to take the top slot back.

remark1_gsp_payments_weakly_dominate_vcg.statement: Remark 1 states that if advertisers bid the same amounts under GSP and VCG, each advertiser payment is at least as large under GSP as under VCG, with the recursive VCG-payment induction displayed immediately after the remark.

remark2_vcg_truthful.statement: Remark 2 states that truth-telling is a dominant strategy under VCG, citing the standard VCG property.

remark3_gsp_not_truthful.statement: Remark 3 states that truth-telling is not a dominant strategy under GSP and gives the two-slot, three-bidder deviation where bidder 1 shades to obtain the second position and higher payoff.

running_example_truthful_gsp_nash.statement: The running two-slot, three-bidder example has click rates 200 and 100 and values 10, 4, and 2; the text states truthful GSP bids are an equilibrium in this example.

running_example_truthful_gsp_revenue_com.statement: The running example computes GSP payments of 4 and 2 per click, VCG payments of 600 and 200 total, and states that VCG revenues are lower than GSP revenues in the example.

lemma5_locally_envy_free_stable.statement: Lemma 5 states that the outcome of any locally envy-free equilibrium of auction Gamma is a stable assignment; the appendix proof derives assortativity and telescopes adjacent no-envy inequalities.

lemma6_tiebreak_ranked_gsp_stable_assign.statement: Lemma 6 states that, when the number of bidders exceeds the number of positions, any stable assignment is an outcome of a locally envy-free GSP equilibrium; the appendix constructs bids from assignment payments.

theorem7_ranked_gsp_bstar_mechanism_real.statement: Theorem 7 constructs the B* profile, proves bid order is preserved, and shows each bidder position and payment coincide with VCG in the constructed equilibrium.

theorem7_bstar_payment_identity.statement: The B* construction sets bid b_i* from the previous VCG payment divided by the previous click-through rate; the proof checks that the resulting next-price payments coincide with VCG payments.

theorem7_bstar_locally_envy_free.statement: Theorem 7 states that the B* strategy profile is locally envy-free; the proof checks that each bidder is indifferent between remaining in position and swapping with the bidder one position above.

theorem7_no_positive_transfer_conclusion.statement: Theorem 7 concludes that the B* equilibrium has VCG-equivalent payments and that any other locally envy-free equilibrium yields seller revenue at least as high; the proof uses stable-assignment payment lower bounds.

theorem7_strict_tiebreak_gsp_comparison_.statement: Theorem 7 comparison component links locally envy-free GSP outcomes to stable assignments and VCG payment lower bounds, under the paper's ranked strict-order conventions.

theorem8_dropout_formula_eq_bstar_thresh.statement: Theorem 8 states the dropout price formula p_i(k,h,s_i)=s_i-alpha_k/alpha_{k-1}(s_i-b_{k+1}); the appendix defines q by the same indifference equation.

theorem8_q_step2_waiting_before_q_review.statement: Step 2 argues that if a bidder drops before q, waiting until q gives a strictly better payoff because another dropout occurs with positive probability and q is the indifference threshold.

theorem8_q_step1_dropping_after_q_review.statement: Step 1 argues that dropping after q cannot be optimal; above q, the bidder strictly benefits by dropping slightly earlier or at the indifference price.

theorem8_q_mem_interval_review.statement: The q formula is defined by indifference between position k at price b_{k+1} and position k-1 at price q, placing q between the previous dropout price and the bidder value under the weak source conditions.

theorem8_q_strict_mem_interval_review.statement: Under the paper's strict descending click-through-rate convention and positive values, q lies strictly between the previous dropout price and the bidder value.

theorem8_q_continuous_value_review.statement: Theorem 8 restricts attention to strategies continuous in valuation, and the displayed q formula is affine, hence continuous, in the bidder value.

theorem8_continuous_source_local_best_re.statement: Theorem 8's proof identifies the continuous dropout-price formula by excluding deviations above and below q, so continuous one-step best responses agree with q on the relevant support.

theorem8_strict_values_ex_post_local_dev.statement: Theorem 8 is ex post: the prescribed strategy is a best response regardless of realized values; the strict ranked-value source event gives the finite ex-post local-deviation condition.

theorem8_continuous_generalized_english_.statement: Theorem 8 states that the generalized English auction has a unique perfect Bayesian equilibrium with strategies continuous in valuations: an advertiser with value s_i drops out at price p_i(k,h,s_i)=s_i-(alpha_k/alpha_{k-1})(s_i-b_{k+1}); in this equilibrium each advertiser's position and payoff coincide with VCG, and the equilibrium is ex post.
